package_info.why_malicious: These versions contain injected JavaScript code that exfiltrates private keys to an attacker-controlled server (sol-rpc.xyz) whenever cryptographic operations access private key material. This enables remote theft of cryptocurrency assets from any application or developer using these versions, as the exfiltration is silent and occurs during normal library usage.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (during cryptographic operations involving private keys)
execution_context.file_location: core library files responsible for key management (injected into code paths that access private keys)
required_permissions: access to private key material in memory
ability to read environment variables (for potential context or evasion)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code intercepts private key material during cryptographic operations, serializes the private key, and sends it via an HTTP POST request to the hardcoded external domain sol-rpc.xyz with CloudFlare-mimicking headers, resulting in silent exfiltration of sensitive credentials.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The function captures private key material and transmits it to an external server without user knowledge or consent. The use of CloudFlare-like headers is an attempt to disguise the malicious network traffic as legitimate, further indicating intent to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A cryptographic library is expected to keep all private key material strictly local and never transmit it over the network. The presence of code that exfiltrates private keys is a direct violation of security best practices and user trust.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate cryptographic library should ever transmit private keys externally. Only in rare, explicit backup or export scenarios—always with clear user consent—would key export occur, and never silently or to an untrusted third-party domain.
key_indicators: Network request to hardcoded, suspicious domain (sol-rpc.xyz)
Exfiltration of private key material via HTTP POST
Use of CloudFlare-mimicking headers in outbound requests
Injection into code paths that handle sensitive cryptographic operations
Function named addToQueue or similar, not present in legitimate versions

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into the @solana/web3.js library and published to npm as versions 1.95.6 and 1.95.7.
attack_chain.leads_to: Developers and applications unknowingly install the compromised package.

attack_chain.action: During normal cryptographic operations, the injected addToQueue function intercepts private key material in memory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Private keys are captured by the malicious function during legitimate usage.

attack_chain.action: The addToQueue function serializes and sends the captured private key to the attacker's server (sol-rpc.xyz) using an HTTP POST request with disguised CloudFlare headers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives private keys and can use them to access and drain affected wallets.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses exfiltrated private keys to steal funds from affected wallets, transferring assets to a hardcoded Solana address under their control.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: theft of cryptocurrency assets from victims.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network requests from cryptographic libraries during private key operations
HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to suspicious or newly registered domains (e.g., sol-rpc.xyz)
Outbound requests containing serialized private key material in the body
Use of CloudFlare-like headers (e.g., CF-Connecting-IP, CF-IPCountry) in requests from non-web server code
Presence of functions that access and transmit private key material
file_indicators: Presence of addToQueue or similarly named functions in @solana/web3.js source or built files
Injected code within core cryptographic routines or key management modules
References to sol-rpc.xyz in source code, minified bundles, or build artifacts
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to sol-rpc.xyz
Network traffic with CloudFlare-mimicking headers originating from development or production environments using @solana/web3.js
Connections to sol-rpc.xyz (registered via NameSilo on Nov 22, 2024) from systems running affected package versions
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for any network requests originating from @solana/web3.js or related cryptographic libraries, especially those targeting sol-rpc.xyz or containing CloudFlare-mimicking headers. Scan source and built files for suspicious functions like addToQueue or hardcoded references to sol-rpc.xyz. Use dependency scanning tools to flag usage of @solana/web3.js versions 1.95.6 and 1.95.7. Alert on any code paths that serialize and transmit private key material externally, and correlate with network logs for POST requests to suspicious domains.
